analysis: Gram-Schmidt is the largest training ratio and samples predominantly in its generated numeric loop. Previously verified instruction sites show comparisons, stack traffic and indexed memory operations. Investigate repeated geometry/check traffic in that native path.

MVT and BiCG are the next largest ratios and spend more than half of sampled execution in allocation plus schema/memory validation. Test general root matrix-expression batching and canonical ownership reuse on the optimization set.
Correlation has substantial runtime helper/control/collection and resource-bookkeeping costs; avoid assuming its primary cost is arithmetic.

ATAX and the dense products also show shared numeric operation setup and owner work; several short kernels yield only27-45 execution samples, so percentages are coarse directions rather than precise cost attribution.
constraints: Largest saved Mech/C margins determine priority. The primary training score is the equal-weight geometric mean, not sum time. Absolute medians are supplied as context.
Profiles reuse exactly the accepted31 driver and frozen program inputs. Diagnostic process times and samples never enter performance scores.
Preserve the fixed15/15 split, all ports/C binaries/flags/limits/tolerances/timing boundaries, and every candidate regression. No holdout per-case profiling or tuning.
